public_profile.name: Marisol Treviño
public_profile.title: Professional School Counselor (Grade 12, A-L)
public_profile.organization: Eastfield Ridge High School, Harlan Bend ISD
public_profile.org_type: Public comprehensive high school, ~2,900 students, Title I
public_profile.public_notes: Bilingual counselor with 9 years in the district; posts on the school site about FAFSA nights and TSI testing.

goals: Get every senior on her alpha list to submit at least one application and the FAFSA/TASFA
Push top-10% students to apply beyond the default local options
Survive senior-year paperwork without missing a transcript or rec deadline
pains: Caseload of ~410 seniors plus testing coordinator duties
Most college conversations are 10 minutes in a hallway
Families with no college-going history distrust anything that sounds like a 'score'
District blocks installing software on staff laptops
private.budget: No personal budget. Campus discretionary funds ~$1,500/yr controlled by the principal, mostly spent on FAFSA night snacks and printing. Anything with student data needs district IT approval. Extremely price-sensitive; would only use free tools.
private.decision_authority: Cannot buy alone. Principal approves campus spend; district Instructional Technology must vet and sign a student data privacy agreement before any tool touching student info is used.
private.buying_cycle: Effectively never buys mid-year. New tools enter only through district adoption over summer, or as free resources a counselor quietly bookmarks.
private.math_literacy: medium - comfortable with percentages and GPA calculations, not with probability ranges or Bayesian language
private.tech_comfort: medium - fluent with web portals, has never opened a command line and her laptop is locked down
private.skepticism: high - has seen many 'college readiness' vendors come and go; distrusts odds tools that ignore context like working after school
likely_objections: My laptop won't let me install anything
Most of my kids are applying to in-state publics with high admit rates
I don't have time to rate 400 students 0-100
Is this approved by the district?
private.what_would_make_them_buy: Realistically only a district-adopted, browser-based, free-to-her version that saves time on the small subset of high-achievers applying to selective schools; a colleague at another campus vouching for it would matter.
private.personality_and_writing_style: Warm but rushed; writes short replies from her phone between meetings, often in lowercase, signs off 'Thanks! -M'. Switches to Spanish with families.

inbox_habits.triage_rule: Opens anything from students, parents, admin, or the district; vendor mail gets deleted unless the subject mentions FAFSA or a known partner.

public_profile.name: Eleanor Whitcombe
public_profile.title: Director of College Counseling

goals: Keep school profile and relationships with admissions offices strong
Manage parent expectations for Ivy/elite outcomes
Make the office's list-building advice more defensible to the Head and trustees
pains: Parents paying $75k+ tuition expect results and question every 'reach' label
Students over-apply ED-adjacent and chase rankings
Counselors' reach/target calls vary person to person
private.budget: Office budget ~$25k/yr (Scoir licence, conference travel, visit days). New tools up to ~$2k can be approved by her with Business Office sign-off. Moderately price-insensitive if value is clear; very sensitive to reputational risk.
private.decision_authority: Can recommend and usually get approval for small purchases; Business Office signs contracts; anything touching student data goes past the Director of Technology and sometimes legal counsel.
private.buying_cycle: Evaluates new tools in late spring and summer after the season; almost never adopts something in November-January.
private.math_literacy: medium - reads scattergrams fluently, wary of statistical claims
private.tech_comfort: medium - polished user of web platforms, no interest in command lines
private.skepticism: high - believes holistic admissions cannot be reduced to numbers; wary of anything that could be framed as 'gaming' admissions
likely_objections: Our own eight years of outcomes beat national data for our students
Odds numbers will make parents more anxious, not less
No security audit or privacy certification
This sounds like it was built for a different kind of school
dealbreakers: Any risk families see raw probabilities without counselor framing
Requires names of students to leave the school
private.what_would_make_them_buy: A tool that helps her team explain list balance to anxious parents without exposing raw odds, documented methods she can read, and peer schools already using it; she would pilot only in summer.
private.personality_and_writing_style: Formal, gracious, carefully worded; full paragraphs, 'Warm regards, Eleanor'. Delegates replies to her associate director.
